findings.reason: a dispatched node would implement four bullet points, watch the hand-resume arm fail, and either drop the arm or invent a fifth change outside its brief.
findings.text: s22 cites "dispose refuses a review that names the pre-repair head" but none of its four changes touches that refusal (they are: finding ids from `repair.finding_id`, the worker's self-check, a three-round resume, and the escalation obligation), while the done-when's sixth arm requires "a run repaired by a hand resume is still reviewable" — so the node can implement all four changes and still fail an arm its own mechanism never addresses

findings.reason: without an edge one of the two lands a predicate the other then re-derives differently, and §11 declares no write paths for `routing.py`, so the claim machinery will not serialise them either.
findings.text: s19 states "The admission-time check in §11 uses the same per-unit predicate", and both it and §11 (`plan.html:92`) narrow the same gate in `reckon/crew/routing.py`, yet `plan-section-depends-on` carries `s20→s19` and nothing between `s11` and `s19`; s11 and s19 are both `implementable`, so both can be queued in the same beat and edited `routing.py` concurrently

findings.reason: the worker would hit a read-only fence on the one module that holds the refusal it must retire, a second instance of the blocking-on-a-widen failure the section exists to remove.
findings.text: s23's mechanism — "It succeeds when no live run, launched or waiting, claims the path, and records the grant, its reason and that the worker made it" — is implemented in `widen_claim` (`reckon/crew/claims.py:63`), which today refuses any run whose worker process is still alive (`ClaimAmendmentRefusedError`, the `WIDEN_RULE` at `reckon/crew_run_commands.py:1141`), and enforces peer conflicts through `refuse_widen_scope_conflicts` in `reckon/crew/dispatch.py`; the section's write paths list only `crew_run_commands.py`, `dispatch_claims.py` and the review-brief composer

findings.reason: the corrected figure changes a plan field the schedule derives from, and the value is the _document unit's own claim about its content.
findings.text: `plan-effort-hours` is `23.25`, the sum of s1–s7 only, while the section declarations that follow sum to `62.0` (implementable sections alone total `23.5`), and `_remaining_effort_hours` (`reckon/roadmap.py:561`) multiplies that explicit total by remaining progress, so the roadmap and schedule read this plan as roughly 10 hours of work remaining instead of about 23.5

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — every cited symbol and path resolves: `require_plan_reviewed` (`reckon/crew/routing.py:2489`), `review_coverage` (`reckon/crew/plan_review.py:821`), `_readiness_rows` and `_launch_queued` (`reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:1429`, `:198`), `_run_open` (`reckon/crew/review_lifecycle.py:126`), `repair.finding_id` (`reckon/crew/repair.py:86`), `crew widen` (`reckon/crew_run_commands.py:1274`), `reckon/crew/dispatch_claims.py`, `reckon/crew/queue_landing.py`, and the run s25 cites exists at its exact id.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — each of s18–s25 states a measurable arm set plus a negative control that fails when the guard is reverted, and every arm names something a test can observe (a call count, a stored field, a refusal, a pointer present from inside a stubbed dispatch).
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the changed units name no session scratchpad, node-local temporary directory or non-durable path; tests are cited by repository path and the repo's gate logs sit under the run directory.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the new test files and every symbol named in s18–s25 names a mechanism ("reads the roadmap once", "a worker widens to an unclaimed path"), with no plan labels, stage names, ticket numbers or version tags.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — s22's hand-resume arm is not produced by any of its four stated changes, and s23's mechanism lives in a module its write paths omit.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — s18 one cache per pass, s19 a review of the change and a gate scoped to it, s20 carried findings and a review cap, s21 self-composition, s22 the review/repair loop, s23 self-widen, s24 a measuring landing pass, s25 a launched record in full; the multi-bullet sections (s22, s24) are one pipeline with one verdict.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — s19's per-unit gate and s11's admission-time per-unit gate narrow the same predicate in `reckon/crew/routing.py`, and neither section declares a wait on the other.
